lexicon: JUNCTION PAIR — the same two junctions and the same three connections, read the other way
description: The identical graph as 011 — two vertices, three edges, degree sequence [3, 3] — with the second junction traversed in the SAME sense as the first rather than the opposite. One face, Euler characteristic 0, genus 1: the same structure now lives on a torus. Nothing in the graph changed. Only the rotation did. Darts 0 and 1 lie in different regions in 011 and the same region here — the machine-checkable form of the difference.
teaches: Module F: the rotation IS the embedding. Same graph, same degree sequence, different surface — the drift case the degree sequence cannot see, and the reason genus is a reading of the marks rather than a property of them.
